title: Windows Commands
label: Windows Commands
desc: Walk the Windows command line from files and processes to services, registry and PowerShell.

sections.title: Files and Directories
sections.description: Create, inspect, copy and remove files and folders with cmd and PowerShell.

snippets.code:
REM List every entry, including hidden and system files
dir /a
REM Bare full paths of matching files, walking subfolders
dir /s /b *.log

REM Change directory, switching drive when needed
cd C:\Users\ana\Projects
cd /d D:\work

REM Point a temporary drive letter at a UNC share, then drop it
pushd \\fileserver\projects
popd

mkdir C:\backup\2026
copy /y report.docx D:\shared\report.docx

REM /e includes empty folders, /i treats the target as a folder, /h keeps hidden files
xcopy C:\photos D:\backup\photos /e /i /h

REM /mir makes the destination an exact copy, deleting extras, with two retries
robocopy C:\data D:\backup /mir /r:2 /w:2

move /y draft.txt final.txt
del /q *.tmp
rmdir /s /q C:\backup\old

# Create a folder and ignore "already exists"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path C:\logs\2026 -Force

# Files over 100 MB anywhere under C:\logs
Get-ChildItem C:\logs -Recurse -File | Where-Object Length -gt 100MB

Copy-Item .\config.json D:\apps\config.json -Force
Move-Item .\old C:\archive\old
Remove-Item C:\temp\* -Recurse -Force

# Size and modification time for one file
Get-Item .\report.docx | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime

sections.title: Viewing Files
sections.description: Read a file, page through it and pull out matching lines.

snippets.code:
REM Print the whole file to the console
type C:\Windows\win.ini

REM Page through a long file: Space next page, Q quit
more /e C:\logs\setup.log

REM Numbered, case-insensitive matches
find /n /i "error" C:\logs\app.log

REM Search every .config below the current folder
findstr /s /i /n "timeout" *.config

# First and last lines of a file
Get-Content .\setup.log -Head 20
Get-Content .\setup.log -Tail 20

# Follow a growing log until Ctrl+C
Get-Content .\setup.log -Tail 50 -Wait

# Keep only matching lines
Get-Content .\setup.log | Select-String -Pattern 'error' -CaseSensitive

# Compare two files line by line
Compare-Object (Get-Content .\before.txt) (Get-Content .\after.txt)

sections.title: Text Processing
sections.description: Filter, sort, count and rewrite text without leaving the shell.

snippets.code:
REM Sort lines and write the result
sort C:\logs\names.txt > C:\logs\names-sorted.txt

REM Count lines: an empty search string matches every line
find /v /c "" C:\logs\app.log

REM Lines that begin with ERROR
findstr /r /c:"^ERROR" C:\logs\app.log

REM Second comma-separated field of each line, typed at the prompt
for /f "tokens=2 delims=," %A in (users.csv) do @echo %A

# Replace text and write the file back
(Get-Content .\hosts) -replace 'old.example.com', 'new.example.com' | Set-Content .\hosts

# Count server errors in a log
Get-Content .\access.log | Where-Object { $_ -match ' 500 ' } | Measure-Object

# Deduplicate and sort a list
Get-Content .\names.txt | Sort-Object -Unique | Set-Content .\names-sorted.txt

# Split, keep, reshape and export rows
Import-Csv .\users.csv |
  Where-Object Department -eq 'Ops' |
  Select-Object Name, Email |
  Export-Csv .\ops.csv -NoTypeInformation

sections.title: Processes
sections.description: List what is running, inspect command lines and end a process.

snippets.code:
REM Everything running, with session and memory columns
tasklist

REM Filter by image name or PID
tasklist /fi "imagename eq chrome.exe"
tasklist /svc /fi "pid eq 4120"

REM Ask before closing, then force the whole process tree
taskkill /im notepad.exe
taskkill /pid 4120 /f /t

# Top processes by CPU time
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Name, Id, CPU

# Where a process lives and when it started
Get-Process -Name node | Select-Object Id, Path, StartTime

# Full command line, which Get-Process does not expose
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'node.exe'" |
  Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine

Stop-Process -Id 4120 -Force
Wait-Process -Id 4120 -Timeout 30
Start-Process notepad -ArgumentList C:\logs\app.log

sections.title: System Information
sections.description: Collect OS, hardware, disk and account details from one machine.

snippets.code:
REM Full report: OS build, RAM, domain and hotfixes
systeminfo

REM Just the interesting lines
systeminfo | findstr /c:"OS Name" /c:"OS Version" /c:"System Boot Time"

REM Machine name and the account you are using
hostname
whoami

# OS edition, build and last boot
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem |
  Select-Object Caption, Version, BuildNumber, LastBootUpTime

# CPU and physical memory
Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors
Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select-Object Manufacturer, Model, TotalPhysicalMemory

# Fixed disks with free space in GB
Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DriveType = 3" |
  Select-Object DeviceID, @{ Name = 'FreeGB'; Expression = { [math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1) } }

sections.title: Network
sections.description: Check addressing, test connectivity and list listening ports.

snippets.code:
REM Addresses per adapter, then the full picture with DNS and MAC
ipconfig
ipconfig /all

REM Drop the resolver cache after changing DNS records
ipconfig /flushdns

REM Reachability and the path taken
ping -n 4 1.1.1.1
tracert learn.microsoft.com
nslookup github.com 1.1.1.1

REM Which process owns a listening port
netstat -ano | findstr :443

REM Routing table
route print

REM Persistent drive letter to a share
net use Z: \\fileserver\projects /persistent:yes
net use Z: /delete

# Port check with a clear boolean result
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName github.com -Port 443

# DNS answers
Resolve-DnsName github.com -Type A

# Interface addressing without parsing text
Get-NetIPConfiguration | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, IPv4Address, IPv4DefaultGateway

# Listening TCP ports, lowest first
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess

sections.title: Services
sections.description: Inspect, start, stop and change the startup type of Windows services.

snippets.code:
REM List running services
net start

REM Service state, startup type and binary path
sc query Spooler
sc qc Spooler

REM Change startup type; the space after start= is required
sc config Spooler start= auto
sc stop Spooler
sc start Spooler

REM net uses the display name, sc uses the short service name
net stop "Print Spooler"
net start "Print Spooler"

# Running services
Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq 'Running'

# One service in detail
Get-Service -Name Spooler | Select-Object Name, DisplayName, Status, StartType

# Change startup type and restart
Set-Service -Name Spooler -StartupType Manual
Restart-Service -Name Spooler -Force

# Find services by wildcard
Get-Service -Name 'Win*' | Format-Table -AutoSize

sections.title: Registry
sections.description: Read, write and back up configuration stored in the registry.

snippets.code:
REM Read a value
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion" /v ProductName

REM Values that launch at sign-in
reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run

REM Create or overwrite a string value
reg add HKCU\Software\Acme /v Editor /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Tools\editor.exe" /f

REM Remove one value, then the whole key
reg delete HKCU\Software\Acme /v Editor /f
reg delete HKCU\Software\Acme /f

REM Back up and restore a key as a .reg file
reg export HKCU\Software\Acme C:\backup\acme.reg
reg import C:\backup\acme.reg

# Read one value
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion' -Name ProductName

# Create a key, then a value inside it
New-Item -Path HKCU:\Software\Acme -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Acme -Name Editor -Value 'C:\Tools\editor.exe'

# Show everything under a key
Get-ChildItem HKCU:\Software\Acme
Get-ItemProperty HKCU:\Software\Acme

# Installed programs with their versions
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' |
  Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion |
  Sort-Object DisplayName

sections.title: PowerShell
sections.description: Core cmdlets and habits for exploring and scripting with objects.

snippets.code:
# Version and edition
$PSVersionTable

# Find commands and read examples without leaving the shell
Get-Command *-Service
Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Examples

# Inspect what an object actually contains
Get-Process -Id $PID | Get-Member

# Objects flow through the pipeline, so property names matter
Get-ChildItem C:\logs -Filter *.log |
  Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) |
  Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum

Get-Process |
  Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending |
  Select-Object -First 5 Name, WorkingSet64

# Persist results as data
Get-Service | Export-Csv C:\temp\services.csv -NoTypeInformation
